newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope says Lebanon peace crucial for Middle East.
newsitem.headline: Pope says Lebanon peace crucial for Middle East.

text.p: Pope John Paul, who made a historic visit to Lebanon last weekend, said on Wednesday he hoped all sides involved in the country's turmoil would work to maintain the peace.
"Peace is, in a way, the fundamental mission of Lebanon," the Pope said during his weekly general audience in St Peter's Square.

"If it is to carry out this mission, which stems from its cultural and religious complexities, the country has a right for support from all elements that can influence peace in its territory," he added.

During last weekend's 32-hour visit, the 76-year-old Pontiff preached a message of Moslem-Christian reconciliation and independence for Lebanon which galvanised the country and astonished the Moslem majority.
Although the 15-year civil war ended in 1990, Moslem fundamentalist Hizbollah guerrillas continue to fight Israeli troops who hold a strip of Lebanese territory in the south.
The minority Christians complain of the presence of Syrian troops, which are stationed in Lebanon and back the Moslem-dominated government.
The Pope made no reference in his address to reports that Lebanese authorities had been warned of a planned assasination attempt before his arrival in Beirut.
The Pope's trip to Sarajevo in mid-April was marred by the discovery shortly before his arrival of anti-tank mines planted under a bridge on his route into the city. The devices were removed.
